application_bit_scan.interpretation: B13[7:6] are the only near-binary healthy/fault discriminators. The next shift is much smaller and remains high in route93 where B13 is normal, so it is not a cleaner persistent-fault candidate.
application_bit_scan.scope: all 224 application bits B0..B27, healthy route 45 versus mean of dead-EPS d4 and faulted e9 occupancy

interpretation: 0xC0 is a strong Brake-to-FRC arbitration-result/fail-state candidate: healthy pre-brick traffic uses ordinary result IDs such as 0x00 and 0x0B and never asserts B13 bit6, while dead-EPS and multiple post-bootstrap faulted routes overwhelmingly or exclusively use 0xC0.

Do not yet name B13 bit6 alone 'lateral control system unachievable'. Toyota successor diagnostics define the full byte as the lateral-control ID of arbitrated result, so 0xC0 may be a special encoded result/status value.

Route 93 has B13=0x00 throughout while its native cruise-state traffic still includes 0x251=0xE0 (unavailable) and conventional 0x90 latch states. Thus 0xC0 is not the persistent DRCC latch itself; it is more plausibly a Brake-side trigger/input or contemporaneous fail state.
The known 0x081 B11[4] request-loss supervisor is not the persistent fault discriminator: it is clear on 13616/13620 dead-EPS frames and shows the same rare transient assertions in healthy traffic.

known_field.low_six_bits: arbitration-result lateral ID (joined to Toyota Operation FFD 0x5285)
